# What allows a plugin's host call: a flag for this invocation, an entry in
# SNGL_ALLOW naming the plugin's origin, or a line `sngl trust` recorded in the
# user's config file. The three are a union.
env SNGL_GENCACHE=off

# Unasked, refused.
! sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out app/app.sngl
stderr 'may not run sh -c'

# A flag names the plugin by its import path, relative to the root.
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out --allow-command='./pc=sh' app/app.sngl
grep 'ran: \[unset\]' out/index.html

# The grant is the command's prefix: one for a different command is no grant.
! sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out --allow-command='./pc=bash' app/app.sngl
stderr 'may not run sh -c'

# The grant is the plugin's: another package naming the same command is not it.
! sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out --allow-command='./other=sh' app/app.sngl
stderr 'may not run sh -c'

# SNGL_ALLOW names the plugin by its origin, which an ambient grant has to:
# an import path is whatever a repository chooses to call its code. It is
# stripped from every process sngl starts, so the command run here -- which
# prints it -- sees nothing.
env SNGL_ALLOW='eval=dir:/nowhere; command=dir:'$WORK'/app/pc=sh'
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out-env app/app.sngl
grep 'ran: \[unset\]' out-env/index.html

# A blanket grant is a flag only.
env SNGL_ALLOW='all'
! sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out app/app.sngl
stderr 'SNGL_ALLOW: "all" grants everything, which an environment variable may not: pass --allow-all'
env SNGL_ALLOW=

# `sngl trust` records the grant in the user's config, by origin, and a later
# build reads it there.
cd app
sngl trust --allow-command='./pc=sh'
stdout '^recorded in '$WORK'/config/sngl/trust.sngl:$'
stdout '^trust.allow\(origin="dir:'$WORK'/app/pc"\) \{ trust.command\(prefix=\["sh"\]\) \}$'
cd $WORK
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out-config app/app.sngl
grep 'ran: \[unset\]' out-config/index.html

sngl trust --list
stdout '^1  trust.allow\(origin="dir:'$WORK'/app/pc"\) \{ trust.command\(prefix=\["sh"\]\) \}$'

sngl trust --remove 1
stdout '^removed 1  trust.allow\(origin="dir:'$WORK'/app/pc"\)'
! sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out app/app.sngl
stderr 'may not run sh -c'

# --allow-all is a flag for one invocation and is never recorded.
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html -o out-all --allow-all app/app.sngl
grep 'ran: \[unset\]' out-all/index.html
! sngl trust --allow-all
stderr '--allow-all is never recorded'

# There is one import root, the program's directory, and no flag names another.
! sngl check --project=. app/app.sngl
stderr 'unknown flag: --project'

-- app/app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import pc "./pc"

const v = pc.run()

ui.window(title="t") {
    ui.text(value="ran: [{v}]")
}
-- app/pc/pc.sngl --
import gen "sngl:x/gen"

// What the command prints: SNGL_ALLOW as the child sees it.
const func run() string {
    var out = ""
    var p = gen.exec(cmd=["sh", "-c", "printenv SNGL_ALLOW || echo unset"])
    for var line = p.stdout {
        out = out + line
    }
    return out
}
